note: Move NVIDIA PiD out of the model picker into the image upscale dropdown as four plugins, on the mechanism MPI-506 builds. Split from MPI-506 because it is a migration, not an addition: it touches a shipped ModelDef, the flowSdxl4k Flow that declares requiredModels ['sdxl-nsfw','nvidia-pid'] to exercise the multi-model install path, and dev_configs/smoke-evidence.json which gates release:check. Today PiD is all-or-nothing at 16.48GB; as four plugins one path costs ~8.1GB (5.23GB shared gemma encoder + ~2.8GB).

Fabio closed 3a and 3b: a text input and denoise go in the toolbar conditionally when PiD is selected, and he adds the missing pidResolution entries so the existing 1.5/2K/3K/4K radio resolves for PiD. pidVariant disappears with the plugin split. Only 3c (flowSdxl4k requiredModels) stays open, plus one new question - the radio's labels are multipliers but PiD's resolutions are absolute targets.

PiD scoped image-only per Fabio, which turns MPI-506's entry declaration into a tool-scoped one. Answered his 'do I need four workflows' with no: the four branches differ in exactly three literals (unet_name, vae_name, latent_format) and everything else is verbatim-identical, so one workflow with three injected literals drops 43 nodes to ~25. More importantly the four-branch shape BREAKS once weights are optional - unet_name is a folder-listing COMBO and validate_prompt rejects unknown values before execution, with no lazy exemption, so a user holding only one plugin would be rejected at prompt time. It only works today because nvidia-pid installs all four weights.

Recorded why PiD cannot just adopt SeedVR2's multiplier: every checkpoint is 1024_to_4096 and the graph enforces it (input normalised to 1024 via MpiScaledDimensions + MpiCrop divisible_by 16, output latent sized at 4096), so it is a fixed 4x trained at one input size. Named the two candidate techniques with their different failure modes - native-then-downscale (safe, no time saving) vs scale-the-input-keep-4x (fast, off-regime input, needs the bench) - plus a cheap A/B decider. Fabio owns the test.

Fabio decided four separate PiD workflow files rather than one file with three injected literals. Accepted - it removes the hardcoded-name validation break just as well, since each file names only its own weight; the costs are four copies of every shared fix and a workflow-file field on the plugin entry. Also resolved the resolution question by observation rather than bench: the live graph implements technique A, with the 1024/2048/3072 scalers hanging off VAEDecode and any_4 passing 4096 through, so correctness is not in question and the only thing to surface is that 1K costs the same as 4K.

Starting the workflow-generation half: Fabio exported comfy_workflows/raw/nvidia_pid_template.json (26 nodes, single branch, arch VAE titled PiD_VAE so the generator cannot grab the pixel_space loader by mistake). summary: Blocker in 3c RESOLVED: no new mechanism needed. FlowDef.requiredDeps already takes dep ids (MPI-304, head-swap ships it) and dep status is stat-based via the id-agnostic comfy/models/check, so a plugin install unlocks the flow. flowSdxl4k drops nvidia-pid from requiredModels and declares pid-sdxl, vae-sdxl, pid-gemma, comfyui-kjnodes instead - strictly smaller than the ModelDef four-arch union. Cost flagged: loses the deliberate multi-model install exercise.
